newsitem.title: UK: Brazil, South Africa feature on sugar freight mkt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil, South Africa feature on sugar freight mkt.

text.p: London's sugar freight market saw a spate of fresh inquiry sprinkled with fixtures on Friday as shipments from Brazil and South Africa continued to dominate business.
Shipbrokers said CSR fixed 27,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to China for end-June/early July and quoted for a further 30,000 tonnes on the same run for July 1/10.
CSR was also believed to have booked a vessel for a 14,000-tonne bulk cargo from Wyndham to Surabaya for early July but no more details were available.
Mauritius Sugar Syndicate reappeared on the market with an enquiry for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar on its usual run from Port Louis to London for July 4/8.
Vitol quoted for 12,000 tonnes in bulk from Maceio to the Black Sea for June 15/25 and Cargill for 20/25,000 tonnes from Maceio and/or Recife to US Gulf/Atlantic for June/July shipment.
Genoc was in the market with three new orders, quoting for a prompt 14,000 tonnes in bags from Santos to Nigeria and 14/22,000 tonnes in bulk from Thailand to Novorossisk for early July.
It was also open for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Maputo to London for early July.
South Africa Sugar Association was said to have fixed its recent cargo from Durban to Novorossisk for June shipment but details of the rate are not yet known.
Of the day's other reported fixtures, Fiji Sugar Marketing was said to have covered 20,000 tonnes from Fiji to London for early July.
Shipbrokers also cited market talk that Brazilian shippers SIMAB may have fixed 14,000 tonnes in bags from Itajai to Lagos for prompt dates.
